summary: Intermittent NaN-padding on embed payloads causing reranker recall drop and p95 latency spikes
description: Customer reports intermittent drop in reranker recall and sudden p95 latency spikes for their dedicated cluster. Symptoms began after proxy-side upgrade on 2026-03-10; errors are sporadic (~2% of requests) and visible as missing top-k candidates and duplicate suppression where results should be distinct. This ticket tracks investigation, temporary mitigations, and a permanent fix. Impact: some queries return fewer candidates and application-level recall falls by ~12% during incidents; tail latency p95 doubles due to CPU fallback in ANN service.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightQuery account (dedicated) in prod-us-west. 2) Call /v1/embeddings with model=ri-embed-large-v3 for a batch of mixed-length inputs (emoji + long titles). 3) Immediately call rerank endpoint /v1/rerank with those embeddings pinned to reranker=ri-reranker-crossencoder-v1. 4) Observe rerank top-k count occasionally lower than expected and p95 spike on repeated trials. Repro rate ~2% across randomized seed. Repro on curl and SDKs. Sample failing input attached in logs field.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): correlated customer report with internal deploys 2026-03-10 of ingest-proxy. SRE reproduced failure envelope using recorded requests; found NaN values present only when embed protobuf chunk alignment crossed 2KB boundary on the proxy. Hypothesis: proxy chunker had off-by-one and failed to zero-fill remainder of float array, leaving uninitialized memory which serializes as NaN on some replicas. Evidence: repeated runs with instrumented proxy show NaN-inserted payloads at same byte offsets; amplitude correlates with requests containing multi-codepoint emojis and long trailing whitespace. Metric: 'embed.nan_count' metric incremented on affected proxies. Repro rate measured 2.1% on prod-us-west during canary timeframe. ANN index treats NaNs as invalid -> triggers fallback path causing p95 spike and suppressed candidates. Temporary mitigation: route BrightQuery traffic away from affected proxy pool and enable strict validation in embeddings-service to reject NaN payloads (returns 400) to avoid corrupting ann-index. Permanent fix under PR to zero-fill padding and add unit tests and fuzzer for boundary conditions.

resolution: Hotfix deployed: ingest-proxy PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/892) which zero-fills embedding padding and adds sanitizer to protobuf encoder. Canary rollout successful in us-west; full rollout to prod-us-east and prod-us-west completed 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC. Temporary routing for BrightQuery removed after verification. ANN shards affected by NaN insertions must be rebuilt to remove corrupted entries - scheduled maintenance 2026-03-15 02:00-04:00 UTC (low-traffic window). Postmortem and follow-ups: (1) Add unit/fuzz test for embedding chunker boundary cases, (2) Emit 'embed.nan_count' alert with severity P1, (3) Add preflight validation on reranker to reject NaN-containing embeddings and return 400 with descriptive error so clients can retry. Customer compensated with one week of free dedicated capacity as goodwill. Ticket will be closed after index rebuild and one week of clean metrics (embed.nan_count==0).
